sub_themes.sub_theme: Satellite LST versus street-level air temperature

insights.claim: Land-surface temperature can misflag heat hotspots, such as unoccupied industrial roofs, relative to street-level air temperature.
Morning satellite snapshots rank blocks poorly against the afternoon air temperatures that drive health risk.
Satellite LST suits mapping hot surfaces but should not decide where people are at heat risk.
Air temperature models trained on few loggers extrapolate in unsampled land-cover types and need low-confidence flags.
Satellite data cover everywhere but measure the wrong quantity, while ground data measure the right one sparsely.
Advocacy claims of ten-degree tree cooling likely reflect surface temperature, not neighbourhood air temperature.
If cooling becomes meaningful only near forty percent canopy, scattered planting in low-canopy blocks achieves little.
One to two degrees of air cooling, though modest-sounding, may matter for heat illness on extreme days.
Request-based planting programs channel new trees disproportionately to already-green, higher-income neighbourhoods.
Planting equity should be measured as surviving canopy gain per neighbourhood rather than counts of trees planted.
Canopy targets should be set per neighbourhood because a citywide average can leave the hottest areas low.
Co-located low-cost sensors diverging over months indicates drift that one-off offset corrections cannot handle.
A regulatory station several kilometres away may legitimately anchor particulate corrections for a neighbourhood sensor network.
Correcting sensors toward a reference risks erasing genuine local differences, so drift must be separated from signal.
A multi-year community sensor network needs a joint spatial measurement-error correction built with a statistics collaborator.
Community sensor data can be published raw with quality flags before a defensible calibrated tier exists.

adjacent_ideas.claim: Calibrated volunteer sensors could fill logger coverage gaps when modelling citywide air temperature from satellite data.
Lower tree survival in low-canopy blocks may prevent them from ever reaching the canopy level where cooling becomes meaningful.
Neighbourhood canopy targets prioritised by modelled air temperature, not LST, could redirect planting to where people experience heat.
